column1: Elevated inflation reflects adverse supply shocks from the pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine energy shock—classic cost-push forces that, in New Keynesian models (e.g., the NK Phillips Curve described by Galí), worsen the near-term output–inflation trade-off. The Fed’s 50 bp rate hike and start of balance-sheet reduction are consistent with inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson and Woodford) and Taylor-rule style prescriptions to anchor expectations, but tighter policy transmits through the credit channel (Bernanke–Gertler), likely weighing on business fixed investment that is sensitive to financing conditions. Oil-price shocks historically depress growth while lifting prices (VAR evidence), and China’s lockdowns exacerbate supply-chain constraints, reinforcing near-term inflation and activity headwinds. Strong household spending and a robust labor market provide some buffer, yet the literature implies net downside risks to real activity with inflation moderating only gradually. sentiment score = -0.25
